ARTICLE III: MEMBERSHIP

Section 1. Eligibility. Membership in the Union shall be open to any person who resides within the Ewu community or its environs, or who is employed by an employer located within the Ewu community, and who is of good character and agrees to abide by the provisions of this Charter and the Bylaws.

Section 2. Application. Application for membership shall be made in writing on a form provided by the Union. The application shall be considered by the Board of Directors or by a Membership Committee appointed by the Board, and approval shall require a majority vote of the members of the Board or Committee present and voting.

Section 3. Share Subscription. Each applicant, upon approval of membership, shall subscribe to at least one share of the Union, of the par value of Ten Naira (₦10.00), and shall pay the par value thereof upon admission.

Section 4. Termination. Membership shall terminate upon the death of the member, upon the member's written resignation, or upon expulsion for cause by a two-thirds vote of the Board of Directors, provided the member has been given notice and an opportunity to be heard.

ARTICLE IV: SHARES

Section 1. Par Value. The par value of each share shall be Ten Naira (₦10.00). No member shall hold shares of the par value of more than Five Thousand Naira (₦5,000.00), except as otherwise provided in the Bylaws.

The Ewu-Edo Community Cooperative Credit Union charter states that the founding year is 1985. Record status: historical.

Section 2. Transfer. Shares shall be transferable only to persons eligible for membership, and only with the approval of the Board of Directors.

Section 3. Withdrawal. A member may withdraw his or her shares upon written notice, subject to the right of the Board of Directors to require a waiting period not exceeding sixty (60) days, and subject to such conditions as may be prescribed in the Bylaws.

ARTICLE V: SAVINGS DEPOSITS

The Union may accept savings deposits from members. Such deposits shall be repayable on demand, subject to such notice and conditions as the Board of Directors may prescribe. Interest on savings deposits shall be paid at a rate determined by the Board of Directors, subject to any applicable law or regulation.

ARTICLE VI: LOANS

Section 1. Authority. The Union may make loans to members from the funds of the Union, including its share capital and savings deposits, subject to the provisions of this Charter, the Bylaws, and any applicable law.

Section 2. Purpose. Loans may be made for provident and productive purposes, including but not limited to: educational expenses, medical expenses, funeral expenses, purchase of household goods, agricultural inputs, small business capital, and housing improvements.

Section 3. Security. Loans shall be made on such security as the Board of Directors may require, including but not limited to: the borrower's shares, co-maker guarantees, chattel mortgages, or other acceptable collateral.

Section 4. Interest. Interest on loans shall be charged at a rate not exceeding one percent (1%) per month on the unpaid balance, or such other rate as may be approved by the Board of Directors and permitted by law.

(e) To provide such other financial services as may be approved by the Board of Directors and permitted by law.

ARTICLE III: MEMBERSHIP

Section 1. Eligibility. Membership in the Union shall be open to any person who resides within the Ewu community or its environs, or who is employed by an employer located within the Ewu community, and who is of good character and agrees to abide by the provisions of this Charter and the Bylaws.

Section 2. Application. Application for membership shall be made in writing on a form provided by the Union. The application shall be considered by the Board of Directors or by a Membership Committee appointed by the Board, and approval shall require a majority vote of the members of the Board or Committee present and voting.

Section 3. Share Subscription. Each applicant, upon approval of membership, shall subscribe to at least one share of the Union, of the par value of Ten Naira (₦10.00), and shall pay the par value thereof upon admission.

Section 4. Termination. Membership shall terminate upon the death of the member, upon the member's written resignation, or upon expulsion for cause by a two-thirds vote of the Board of Directors, provided the member has been given notice and an opportunity to be heard.

ARTICLE IV: SHARES

Section 1. Par Value. The par value of each share shall be Ten Naira (₦10.00). No member shall hold shares of the par value of more than Five Thousand Naira (₦5,000.00), except as otherwise provided in the Bylaws.

The Ewu-Edo Community Cooperative Credit Union charter states that the founding year is 1985. Record status: historical.

Section 2. Transfer. Shares shall be transferable only to persons eligible for membership, and only with the approval of the Board of Directors.

Section 3. Withdrawal. A member may withdraw his or her shares upon written notice, subject to the right of the Board of Directors to require a waiting period not exceeding sixty (60) days, and subject to such conditions as may be prescribed in the Bylaws.

ARTICLE V: SAVINGS DEPOSITS

The Union may accept savings deposits from members. Such deposits shall be repayable on demand, subject to such notice and conditions as the Board of Directors may prescribe. Interest on savings deposits shall be paid at a rate determined by the Board of Directors, subject to any applicable law or regulation.

ARTICLE VI: LOANS

Section 1. Authority. The Union may make loans to members from the funds of the Union, including its share capital and savings deposits, subject to the provisions of this Charter, the Bylaws, and any applicable law.

Section 2. Purpose. Loans may be made for provident and productive purposes, including but not limited to: educational expenses, medical expenses, funeral expenses, purchase of household goods, agricultural inputs, small business capital, and housing improvements.

Section 3. Security. Loans shall be made on such security as the Board of Directors may require, including but not limited to: the borrower's shares, co-maker guarantees, chattel mortgages, or other acceptable collateral.

Section 4. Interest. Interest on loans shall be charged at a rate not exceeding one percent (1%) per month on the unpaid balance, or such other rate as may be approved by the Board of Directors and permitted by law.

been issued to staff. Compliance had improved, though one staff member
had been cautioned in writing for repeated lateness.
b) Loan Disbursement Procedures: The Treasurer reported that the
fourteen working day processing period was being observed. Two loan
applications received in the first week of April had been processed
within the stipulated period.

Board received a report from the Building Committee.

The Board considered a report from the Secretary on the number of
membership applications received since the commencement of operations.

applicants, subject to the payment of the registration fee and the
first share contribution.

The Board deliberated on the need to set a maximum limit for loans to
individual members. After consideration, the Board resolved as follows:

EWU-EDO COMMUNITY COOPERATIVE CREDIT UNION

P. O. Box 214, Ewu, Edo State

ANNUAL REPORT FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31ST DECEMBER, 1985
Presented at the First Annual General Meeting
Held at the Ewu Town Hall on 15th February, 1986

1. INTRODUCTION

This report covers the activities of the Credit Union from its registration on 1st March, 1985 to 31st December, 1985. The Union commenced operations with forty-eight founding members and has grown steadily during the year. The Board is pleased to present this report to the members and to the Local Government Department of Cooperatives for the year under review.

2. MEMBERSHIP

During the year under review, the Union admitted forty-one new members, bringing the total membership to eighty-nine as at 31st December, 1985. The breakdown of membership is as follows:

| Category | Number |
|----------|--------|
| Founding members (March 1985) | 48 |
| Members admitted April – June | 12 |
| Members admitted July – September | 16 |
| Members admitted October – December | 13 |
| Total | 89 |

All members have fulfilled the requirements of the Bye-Laws with respect to registration fees and share contributions. The Board wishes to note that the rate of membership growth exceeded expectations, and this has necessitated the appointment of an additional Assistant Treasurer to handle the increased volume of share contributions and savings collections.

3. SHARE CAPITAL AND SAVINGS

The total share capital as at 31st December, 1985 stood at N12,340.00. Members' savings deposits during the year amounted to N28,765.50, of which N20,920.00 was withdrawn by members for various purposes permitted under the savings policy. The balance of savings deposits as at the end of the year was N7,845.50.

The Board notes with concern that the level of savings withdrawals during the latter part of the year was higher than anticipated. The Board has therefore directed the Savings Committee to review the withdrawal procedures and to ensure that members are properly advised of the benefits of regular savings.

4. LOANS

The total amount disbursed as loans during the year was N18,450.00. A total of fifty-seven loans were granted to members for various purposes, including the purchase of grinding machines, trading capital, school fees, and home improvements. The loan portfolio as at 31st December, 1985 is summarized below:

| Purpose | Number of Loans | Amount Disbursed (N) |

The Board wishes to report that loan repayments have been generally satisfactory. As at 31st December, 1985, a total of N11,275.00 had been repaid, leaving an outstanding balance of N7,175.00. However, the Board notes that three loans are in arrears and the Loan Officer has been directed to take appropriate steps to recover these amounts.

5. FINANCIAL POSITION

The audited financial statements for the year ended 31st December, 1985 are attached to this report. The summary of the financial position is as follows:

| Loan fund | 18,450.00 |
| Loans outstanding | 7,175.00 |

| Cash in hand | 1,275.50 |
| Reserve fund | 1,200.00 |
| Income (interest and fees) | 1,845.00 |
| Expenditure | 1,210.00 |
| Surplus for the year | 635.00 |

An emergency meeting of the entire membership was convened on Tuesday, 2nd June, 1987, at the Ewu-Edo Primary School premises. The meeting was called to address the reported theft of the Society’s cash box which occurred on the night of 30th May, 1987, from the temporary office at the back of Mr. O. O. Egharevba’s shop.

The Chairman, Mr. S. O. Obaseki, informed members that the total sum stolen was N2,340.50, comprising contributions collected for the building fund. The Police Post at Ewu-Edo has been informed and a report obtained. Members expressed concern over the security of funds and resolved as follows:

- That a metal safe be purchased immediately at a cost not exceeding N350.00.
- That the cash box be kept henceforth in the residence of the Treasurer, subject to a bond of N500.00 being executed by him.
- That all cash collections be banked within 24 hours of receipt, except where the bank is closed.
